## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Isolated Action runs could fail command lookups and Git checks even when the tools and checkout were available: inaccessible runner-owned PATH directories caused `EACCES` instead of `ENOENT`, and Git rejected the runner-owned checkout when system and global config were disabled. The Action now filters PATH entries to directories the agent can enter and passes the checkout as `safe.directory` through environment-based Git configuration.

Real-runner coverage now checks both missing-command behavior and checkout trust when `HOME`, global Git config, and system Git config are overridden. These changes address 14 of the 15 false failures observed in the remediation job; the remaining failure was not explained by the probe and is not addressed here. [#2222](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2222)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

Isolated agents now have their own XDG data, config, cache, and state directories under their home, preventing tools that follow XDG from writing into read-only runner directories. Each directory’s `opencode` entry links back to the runner-provided location, so the server’s database, logs, and configuration remain there while other tools keep their own data with the agent. This also lets XDG-aware tools such as pnpm use their standard locations without separate environment-variable overrides.

The change preserves the existing runner paths for session recovery and cache saving, and keeps bun’s cache explicitly configured because it does not follow XDG. The setup now requires `ln`, and the real-runner checks cover pnpm’s store and writes to XDG cache and data locations. [#2219](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2219)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

When `isolate-agent` is enabled, agents can now run Bun and pnpm installed in the runner’s home, without receiving write access to those installation roots. The action grants read/execute access only to qualifying runner-owned directories on the agent’s `PATH`, and rejects grants that would expose sensitive or writable locations.

Python package workflows are also isolated from the runner’s read-only XDG directories: uv and pip caches, managed Python installations, and tool installations now live under the agent’s own home. Project virtual environments remain in the checkout, and these environment changes do not apply when isolation is disabled. [#2217](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2217) [#2218](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2218)

Successful isolation checks are now visible in info-level logs: the preflight read-only view probe reports its pass and elapsed time, and sandbox teardown reports when the launch namespace is confirmed empty. Failure reporting is unchanged, and these success logs are emitted only when `isolate-agent` is enabled. [#2215](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2215)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

When `isolate-agent` is enabled, the agent now runs inside a private filesystem view that makes shared runner mounts read-only while keeping required locations—such as the checkout, session storage, and agent home—writable. Startup checks the view before launching the agent, and teardown verifies that processes in its mount namespace are gone before allowing the run to continue. The sandbox also receives the runner's existing `PATH`, so tools installed earlier in the workflow can be found; the sandbox-off behavior is unchanged. [#2209](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2209) [#2213](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2213)

The Hono updates address security issues in request validation, body buffering, mounted-path forwarding, and static-file path decoding. The fixes prevent malformed content types from bypassing validation, chunked bodies from accumulating unbounded per-chunk overhead, and encoded paths from reaching files or routes outside the intended path; the static-server fix also covers `allowPercentInPath`. [#2203](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2203) [#2204](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2204)

## What's new
<!-- fro-bot-narration-v1 -->

The Action now runs OpenCode V2 2.3.0, bringing background subagents that return a session ID immediately and report back when idle. The update also adds experimental MCP event support and preserves shell-command output across server handoffs. [#2189](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2189)

Isolated runs can now push through the GitHub token already provisioned to the sandbox user, without enabling checkout credential persistence or exposing credentials on triggers where they are withheld. Isolation also creates the agent's home without copying the runner's large `/etc/skel` contents, and captures a bounded, private snapshot of this run's logs only after sandbox take-back; if isolation was requested but the sandbox never started, logs are not published. [#2202](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2202) [#2208](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2208) [#2201](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2201)

The security guidance for `isolate-agent` now clarifies both its value and its limit: it is recommended for runs with write-capable tokens, but is hardening rather than a security boundary while shared runner directories remain writable by the agent. The docs point to a two-job pattern when a token must be protected, and the input remains opt-in. [#2198](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2198) [#2206](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2206)

Successful key-proxy startup probes and confirmed proxy stops now produce explicit, tested log messages, making those outcomes observable without logging response bodies or credentials. [#2195](https://github.com/fro-bot/agent/pull/2195)
